claim: After a move Build (Blood's ENGINE_19960925 path) picks the mover's sector as the first entry of clipsectorlist that contains the point IN PLAN, without consulting z; the list is seeded with the mover's own sector and only walls inside a box reaching move + MAXCLIPDIST (1024) + walldist + 8 either side of the move's centre are examined (2,264 either side for a 1,024-unit move, our CLIP_RADIUS). So two sectors overlapping in plan are confusable only when they are portal neighbours within that box; rooms stacked one above the other with the way between them going out to a stairwell are safe at zero plan distance.
evidence: NBlood/source/build/src/clip.cpp:1112-1121 (clipmove_compat, called from clipmove at :1824 outside ENGINE_EDUKE32 mode), :1500 (clipmove: rad), :1508 (clipmove: clipsectorlist[0] = own sector), engine_priv.h:19 MAXCLIPDIST 1024; tools/mine_layers.py:54 CLIP_RADIUS 2,264.

Over 2,614 campaign overlap pairs: 16.4% clash in z, 0.19% are confusable, and one pair (E1M1 45/55, a self-touching loop) is both (tools/mine_layers.py, knowledge/blood/design/layers-v1.json, 2026-08-28). A first rule of '5 portal hops' from the campaign median fired falsely on every small stacked building.
use: Stack enclosed rooms by plan overlap freely; forbid only a portal-neighbour overlap that also clashes in z. bloodmap.layers enforces exactly that conjunction.
